title: SQL object assessment and first extraction-procedure port

selection.reason: The real procedure reads Orders, OrderLines and Customers, already in the current warehouse. Its only additional data lookup is the 14-row Warehouse.PackageTypes reference. Website.SearchForCustomers also needs Cities and People, and is deferred.
selection.scope: One read/extraction contract. No write procedure, source procedure replacement or application cutover.

parameters: last_cutoff: ISO datetime2(7) text without timezone; NULL allowed
reference_version: explicit loaded PackageTypes snapshot identifier
contract.window: Last Modified When > last_cutoff AND Last Modified When <= new_cutoff. Last Modified When is the source CASE expression choosing the newer order/line edit time. NULL, equal and reversed cutoff windows return no rows.
contract.time_precision: Normalize to YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffffff text, comparing with C collation. Keep the seventh fractional digit. Strip the Debezium serializer Z only from archived source values; do not convert wall clocks across timezones. The public ISO contract is narrower than arbitrary T-SQL date coercions.
contract.result: Preserve all 18 source column names and values. SQL date results remain date; Last Modified When is exact ISO text rather than a six-digit PostgreSQL timestamp. Source success code 0 becomes a successful SELECT result; this is not T-SQL wire-protocol compatibility.
contract.numeric: Use fixed decimal casts matching the observed SQL Server 16 / compatibility 130 expression types: quantity*price decimal(29,2); multiplying by tax decimal(38,5); division and rounded tax numeric(38,6); total including tax numeric(38,6). Preserve NULL prices and half-away-from-zero rounding, including negative quantities. The tested source engine truncates the division result to six fractional places before the final ROUND. Migration 004 reproduces that step; it avoids an extra cent for quantity=1, price=0.01 and tax=49.999.
contract.ordering: OrderID ascending with a deterministic OrderLineID tie-breaker in the target. Source tie order is unspecified, so validation compares duplicate-preserving row multisets within OrderID groups. Add an outer ORDER BY when composing a consumer query.
contract.reference: Load an immutable, content-addressed PackageTypes snapshot with checksum, source capture time and temporal bounds. Pass its version explicitly; unknown, incomplete or missing-key snapshots fail. There is no automatic refresh and no new CDC capture generation.
contract.current_state: Use current non-deleted warehouse rows, as the source procedure queries current source tables. The procedure does not emit deletions or previous historical versions. Customer/reference changes alone do not advance its order/line edit cutoff.

security.source: The procedure runs WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER. The source has an enabled customer RLS policy involving city/territory membership.
security.target: SECURITY INVOKER; pinned pg_catalog search path; schema-qualified relations; PUBLIC execution revoked. Only warehouse_reader receives usage/SELECT/EXECUTE. The CDC loader receives no API or reference-write privilege.
security.certified_scope: Full-scope lab reader only. Per-application identity, territory restrictions, external callers and ownership remain unconfirmed; do not infer application authorization parity from row equality.

assessment.method: Definition fingerprints, source metadata, direct/transitive dependency graph, module execution context, parameter types, SQL Agent command fingerprints and heuristic dynamic-SQL flags.
assessment.limitations: SQL schemas/names suggest categories, not proven application ownership. Static dependencies and procedure-cache observations are incomplete; absence from cache does not justify deletion. No object is approved for retirement.

validation.source_execution: Run the original SQL Server procedure, capture its 18-column result into a temporary table, then stream JSONL in one SERIALIZABLE source transaction. Source business data and definitions are unchanged.
validation.target_comparison: Read-only warehouse_reader connection in REPEATABLE READ, server-side cursor, exact Decimal values, ordered groups, duplicate preservation, complete result counts and SHA-256 fingerprints.
validation.limits: Quiet fixture validation only. Source SERIALIZABLE reads can block writers. Not an online cutover checkpoint, deletion feed, purge watermark or capacity certification.

operations.migration: 003-order-updates-api.sql adds the API/reference schemas; 004-order-tax-division.sql corrects intermediate division precision. Both are checksum-ledgered; applied migrations are never edited.
operations.recovery: Protected schema-only backup in /srv/decom-sqlserver/releases/order-updates-v1-20261028, plus the verified PackageTypes bundle. Existing full warehouse recovery evidence remains separate.
operations.disable_api: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION app.get_order_updates(text,text,text) FROM warehouse_reader;
operations.rollback: Disable the API without deleting CDC data or reference history. Use a subsequent numbered migration to correct or retire the implementation; do not edit an applied migration.
